title: Release scope review for the mobile app
covers: inverted-meaning statements: a negation around words a quote can lift
keeping something by saying it is not removed

segments.speaker: Morgan Example
segments.text: Let's go through the release scope for the mobile app.

segments.speaker: Jordan Example
segments.text: I'm not saying we should drop the audit log. We keep it in this release.

segments.speaker: Morgan Example
segments.text: Good. And the mobile app will not ship in March, the store review takes too long.

segments.speaker: Jordan Example
segments.text: Right, we move the mobile launch to April.

segments.speaker: Casey Example
segments.text: I thought we'd cut offline mode?

segments.speaker: Morgan Example
segments.text: No, we're not cutting offline mode. It stays, just behind a flag.

segments.speaker: Casey Example
segments.text: Fine by me. I'll update the release checklist today.

segments.speaker: Morgan Example
segments.text: Hardly anyone uses the legacy sync, but we're not removing it yet.

segments.speaker: Jordan Example
segments.text: Agreed, legacy sync stays until the next major version.

decisions.text: Keep the audit log in this release.
The mobile app will not ship in March.
The mobile launch moves to April.
Offline mode stays, behind a flag.
Legacy sync stays until the next major version.
